# 1 Enoch Chapter 22 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QEn (Aramaic) | **Section:** Book of Watchers

---

**1** From there I traveled to another place. In the west he showed me a great high mountain with a hard cliff face, containing four deep, wide, and perfectly smooth hollows carved into it. Three were pitch-dark; one was bright, with a spring of water flowing through it. I said: "These hollows are incredibly smooth — how deep and dark they are!"

**2** Raphael, the holy angel accompanying me, answered: "These hollows were made for exactly this purpose: to gather together the spirits of all the dead — every soul of every human being who has ever lived."

**3** "They were made to hold those spirits until the day of judgment, until the time appointed for them, until the great final judgment falls upon them."

**4** Then I saw the spirit of a dead man. His voice was crying out toward heaven in urgent appeal.

**5** I asked Raphael: "Whose spirit is this, crying out to heaven like that?"

**6** He told me: "This is the spirit of Abel, killed by his brother Cain. He is crying out against Cain until the last of Cain's descendants is wiped from the face of the earth and his line is cut off from the human race entirely."

**7** Then I asked about all four hollows: "Why is each one kept separate from the others?"

**8** He answered: "These three chambers have been created to separate the spirits of the dead into different groups. The bright chamber with the spring is for the spirits of the righteous."

**9** "The second has been made for sinners who died and were buried without ever being brought to justice in their lifetimes."

**10** "Their spirits will be held in great torment here until the great day of judgment — the day of punishment and everlasting condemnation. On that day they will receive full recompense, and they will be bound there forever."

**11** "The third chamber is for those whose cries rise up to heaven — those who were murdered in the days of sinners, and who bear witness to their own violent deaths."

**12** "And the fourth is for the spirits of godless sinners, those who were thoroughly corrupt. They will not be judged on the final day, nor will they be raised to life — they simply remain there."

**13** Then I blessed the Lord of glory and said: "Blessed be my Lord, the Lord of righteousness, who reigns forever."

**14** From there I traveled on, going east of that mountain until I reached the ends of the earth.

---

*PNEUMA notes: Dynamic equivalence rendering. Chapter 22 is one of the most theologically rich chapters in the Book of Watchers, presenting a fourfold afterlife geography. The four chambers are identified and their populations distinguished for modern readers. Abel's petition (v. 6) is presented dramatically. The distinction between the resurrected and non-resurrected dead (v. 12) is made explicit.*
